literature_proposed.summary: Known in the literature, and since 2026-11-11 reduced in Lean on this record to one cited theorem. The statement says that for large k no n with 2k <= n < k^3 has every prime factor of C(n,k) above k. It follows from Konyagin's theorem g(k) >= exp(c log^2 k) (1999), where g(k) is the least n > k+1 with every prime factor of C(n,k) above k. The earlier record on this node (t1009-c, 2026-10-09) says "A published theorem, not formalised" and that a formal proof needs an explicit bound beating k^3; neither sentence describes the record any more. The node now has a second route (partial merged as pull request #1293): its assembly is proved, and of its five holes four are proved in Lean (the counts on three ranges of n, erdos-1094--h2--h2--h2--h2--h1, erdos-1094--h2--h1--h1--h4, erdos-1094--h2--h1--h1--h5, and the small range erdos-1094--h2--h1--h1--h6); the fifth is the Baker-Harman-Pintz count of primes in (k, k + k^(21/40)), erdos-1094--h2--h2--h1, which is cited and not formalised. The proof is an existence proof and gives no explicit constant. Its argument: a prime p with k/2 < p <= k divides C(n,k) as soon as two multiples of p lie among n-k+1, ..., n; for the primes just above k/2 where that fails, n/p (after a shift) is within a small distance of an integer, and van Doorn and Tang's formalised counting bounds show such p are fewer than the primes Baker, Harman and Pintz supply. This is the case w = 2 of the device Trifonov (1998, section 4.3) reports from Konyagin's proof, counted with denominator 1 after a shift of n: there, a prime p just above k/2 not dividing C(n,k) has n/p just below an integer; here n is first replaced by n - k - floor(K^(21/40)), K = floor(k/2), so that the counts already formalised apply (checked against Trifonov's text by t1111-a and t1111-d). The general case, with products wp and rationals of small denominator, is the node erdos-1094--h2--h2--h4. Konyagin's paper itself has not been read by anyone who worked on this record.
